title: harnesswalk canonical diagram
description: The canonical diagram of the harness. Implementations derive the served diagram from their registered nodes and MUST NOT introduce node or edge ids that are absent here. Referential rules that JSON Schema cannot express (parents exist, edge endpoints exist, walk_order covers every simple node) are listed in spec/harness.md and checked by tests/spec/test_diagram.py.

edges.description: Ordered. Renderers draw edges in this order; simple edges come before expert edges.

walk_order.description: The teaching order: every simple-view node once, in the order a request with a destructive tool call meets them, then the post-turn and ops nodes. Lessons and the default step-mode tour follow it.

paths.description: Expected simple-view node paths (the node_id of each node_enter, simple nodes only, in order) for canonical requests. paths.plain_answer is the sequence a plain request visits.

kind.description: Decides what the inspector shows: code shows source, config shows the config file, prompt shows the prompt or skill text, store shows records, queue shows pending items, model shows models and the routing decision.

parent.description: Required for expert nodes: the simple-view node that contains this one. Absent on simple nodes.

lesson_url.description: Optional (P5): the chapter that teaches this node, a path relative to the repo root, with a #section anchor for an expert node inside its group chapter.

lesson_summary.description: Optional (P5): the one-line hook of the node's lesson, for lists and the lessons drawer.

source_hint.description: Planned module path in the reference implementation, relative to the repo root.

artifact_hint.description: Optional path of the non-code artifact behind the node (config file, prompt, skills, dataset file). <pack> stands for the active dataset pack.

can_disable.description: True when the node can be switched off: for one turn by the UI or the CLI, to demonstrate the failure it prevents (dev and private modes only), or by a harness profile (spec/harness.md section 10; public mode keeps the controls on).

layout.description: Optional fixed position (top-left, diagram units) in the simple view. On an expert child it is the child's place inside its open parent, relative to the parent's top-left. Absent means auto-layout (P2). A renderer may ignore it; node and edge existence never depends on it.

expert.description: Optional fixed position in the advanced view, where parents grow to hold their children. Absent means the simple-view position.

refines.description: Expert edges only: the simple edge this one details. In advanced view the renderer hides a simple edge once any edge refines it.

layout.description: Optional routing hints for the simple view, in the same units as node layout. The renderer draws the edge orthogonally from the source port through the waypoints to the target port. A port sits on the named side where the nearest waypoint projects onto it (the side centre when it does not). On an expert edge the hints are for the advanced view, where a renderer may use only `handles`. Hints are hints: an edge without them is routed automatically.

waypoints.description: Bend points [x, y] between the two ports, in order.

label.description: Which side of the edge's longest segment its label sits on, so a label never covers the line or the dot moving along it.
